headline: Ship a multi-agent portfolio piece from SF and become the local go-to for agentic systems.
why_now: AI Agents and Agentic Workflows are exploding: GitHub and Hugging Face activity are both above 92, project_potential sits at 96, and Bay Area job demand is at 85. With this much momentum in the SF ecosystem, the next 90 days are a rare window to publish a portfolio piece that recruiters and founders actively search for.
study: Read Anthropic's 'Building Effective Agents' and OpenAI's function-calling docs to ground yourself in tool-use patterns.
Build a LangGraph or CrewAI tutorial locally: one planner agent that calls a web search tool, a calculator, and a file writer, with a LangSmith or Phoenix trace of each step.
Reproduce a small open-source agent (e.g., a ReAct research agent) from Hugging Face, swap its tools, and benchmark it on a 20-question task set.
Study MCP (Model Context Protocol) and add at least one MCP server to your agent so it can connect to a real data source.
Write a short eval harness using inspect-ai or simple assertions to grade your agent's tool calls and final answers.

build.title: AgentOps: a self-improving research agent with traceable tool use
build.description: A multi-agent app where a planner agent decomposes a user query, a researcher agent fetches and cites sources, and a critic agent scores outputs and feeds failures back into the planner. The repo ships with a Replay UI that visualizes the trace graph, making it immediately obvious why it stands out.
deliverables: Public GitHub repo with clean README, eval results, and a trace screenshot
Live Replay UI demo on Vercel
Blog write-up on Medium or your personal site with the eval numbers and trace GIF

publish: Post a 60-second Replay UI demo on X and tag @LangChainAI, @crewAIInc, and Bay Area AI builders.
Submit the project to the 'AI Agents' channel on Hugging Face Spaces and share it in the SF AI Agents meetup.
Cold-DM 5 SF founders or hiring managers at LangChain, Anthropic, and Sierra with a 3-bullet summary and the live demo link.
Cross-post the write-up to LinkedIn with a clear hook for AI engineer recruiters in the Bay Area.
skills: Prompt engineering for planners and critics
risks: Agent demos are notoriously flaky; a single bad run can undermine the whole pitch if you do not lock down evals.
Tool API costs can balloon quickly during testing without rate limits and caching.
The space is moving so fast that a pattern you learn today (e.g., raw function calling) may be obsolete within months, so favor abstractions like LangGraph or MCP that absorb the churn.
confidence: Signals are unusually strong and aligned to your profile and location, so this is a high-conviction bet to ship within 6 weeks.
